criteria.evidence: All five guided sections plus ICE are substantive: 'When it runs: the search runs on request, when a person or a play asks for a domain. The keep-out check is part of the spine linter (lint_grounding.py --spine)...'; Inputs name the spine fields, Touches marks, plan file 'tree'/'children'/'kind'/'issue'; Outputs name each error and warning; nine Given/When/Then criteria; Out of scope names /discover-domains, fn-724, fn-725, cap-719.

'A capability names at most one domain; a domain lists its capabilities only through those capability entries, so there is one place to change.' / 'A link the check finds on one side only is a warning for alignment, never an error, and it never stops a write: the parent capability's rule is that nothing is blocked' / 'any of these is an error, because domains set which areas the product covers, not what work is done.'

Discrete bullets throughout; function stated as behavior ('A domain lists the business intents and capabilities in it'), no user story; acceptance in Given/When/Then form: 'Given a capability whose `domain` names an id the spine does not hold, when a search for that id runs, then the capability is listed marked "not in the spine"...'

Parent gives one line: 'the loose links from a domain to its business intents and capabilities, so a search by domain can be answered.' The child adds the two-sided link rule, the 'one-sided' flag, the 'not in the spine' marker, how the check detects a domain issue from files ('a domain entry in the spine that carries an `issue` field ... or a node in a plan file whose `kind` is domain'), and the empty-model case ('domains: []').

What: 'a search by domain lists its business intents and capabilities, and no domain ever appears in a plan or the tracker'. Why: 'A domain is a big area of the product, kept in the model only for finding things.' Edges: 'Out of scope - Writing domain pages ... /discover-domains owns that. Deciding readiness - fn-724 owns it.' A cold reader can explain the node from the doc alone.
